title: Worsening breathlessness at 41 despite quitting smoking
chief_complaint: Breathlessness on exertion that has been getting worse for two years
vignette: A 41-year-old carpenter sees his GP because he now has to stop for breath after one flight of stairs. He smoked 10 cigarettes a day from age 17 and stopped five years ago. Two courses of inhalers for presumed asthma did not help. His father died of 'emphysema' at 52 without ever having smoked heavily.

findings.text: Progressive exertional breathlessness over two years
findings.evidence: he now has to stop for breath after one flight of stairs

findings.text: Morning cough with scant clear sputum
Two courses of inhaled treatment for presumed asthma without benefit
findings.evidence: Two courses of inhalers for presumed asthma did not help

findings.text: Neonatal jaundice that needed phototherapy, according to his mother
Ex-smoker: 10 cigarettes a day from age 17 to 36 (about 10 pack-years)
findings.evidence: He smoked 10 cigarettes a day from age 17 and stopped five years ago

findings.text: Carpenter; drinks about 10 units of alcohol a week
Father died of emphysema at 52 despite light smoking
Hyperinflated chest with reduced breath sounds at both bases
Prolonged expiration; no wheeze and no clubbing
Chest X-ray: hyperinflated lungs with lucent lower zones
CT chest: panlobular emphysema, worst in both lower lobes
Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.52 with no significant bronchodilator reversibility
Genotyping: PiZZ, confirming severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

decisions.prompt: What else do you want to know?
decisions.explanation: Fixed airflow obstruction at 41 after light smoking is out of proportion to the exposure: ask about the dose, the family, the liver and occupational exposure.

options.text: How much did he smoke, and when did he stop?
options.reveal: 10 a day from 17 to 36; none since.

options.text: Any lung or liver disease in the family?
options.reveal: His father died of emphysema at 52; an aunt had liver trouble.

options.text: Any liver problems or jaundice, even as a baby?
options.reveal: His mother says he was jaundiced as a newborn and needed light treatment.

options.text: Any occupational dust or fume exposure?
options.reveal: Sawdust at work; he wears a mask most of the time.

options.text: Does he keep pets at home?
options.feedback: Not relevant to fixed airflow obstruction at this age.
Travel does not explain two years of progressive breathlessness.

decisions.prompt: Which diagnoses do you keep open?
decisions.explanation: Early basal emphysema after light smoking is the classic picture of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency; smoking-related COPD stays open until the serum level is back.

options.feedback: No reversibility and no response to inhaled treatment.
Scant sputum and no crackles make it unlikely; the CT settles it.

decisions.explanation: Spirometry confirms fixed obstruction, CT shows the basal panlobular pattern, and a low serum level followed by phenotyping or genotyping makes the diagnosis; the liver is checked because the same protein accumulates there.

options.reveal: FEV1/FVC 0.52, FEV1 48 % predicted, no significant reversibility.
Panlobular emphysema, worst in both lower lobes.

options.feedback: Cystic fibrosis is unlikely with this history and imaging.
Atopy does not explain fixed airflow obstruction.

decisions.explanation: Basal panlobular emphysema in a light ex-smoker of 41, a father with early emphysema, neonatal jaundice, a raised ALT and a serum level of 0.3 g/L point to severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (PiZZ).
accepted_answers: Emphysema due to alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

decisions.explanation: Treat the COPD component, discuss augmentation therapy at a specialist centre, offer cascade testing to relatives and protect the lungs and liver. Maintenance oral steroids and montelukast add harm or nothing.

options.text: Long-acting bronchodilators (LAMA plus LABA) and pulmonary rehabilitation
Refer to a specialist centre to discuss intravenous augmentation therapy
Offer testing to his siblings and children
Pneumococcal and annual influenza vaccination; keep alcohol low and monitor the liver

options.feedback: Maintenance oral corticosteroids add osteoporosis, diabetes and infection risk without slowing emphysema.
There is no asthma here; it adds nothing.
